title: Differential Equations: The Language of Nature

blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Equations with Derivatives
blocks.content: A regular equation gives you a number: x + 3 = 7, so x = 4. A **Differential Equation** gives you a function! It contains derivatives (like dy/dx) and your job is to find the original function y. Differential equations describe how things change: population growth, radioactive decay, electrical circuits, even the spread of diseases.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: Order and Degree
blocks.content:
• The **Order** of a DE is the highest derivative present. If it contains dy/dx, it's 1st order. If it contains d^2y/dx^2, it's 2nd order.
• The **Degree** is the power of the highest derivative (after removing fractions and roots).
• A **General Solution** contains an arbitrary constant C.
• A **Particular Solution** uses initial conditions to find the exact value of C.

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Solving by Separation of Variables
blocks.content:
For equations where you can separate x and y:

1. Move all y terms and dy to one side.
2. Move all x terms and dx to the other side.
3. Integrate both sides.
4. Don't forget to add the constant of integration C!
5. If given initial conditions (like y=2 when x=0), substitute to find C.

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Separable DE
blocks.content:
Solve dy/dx = 2x, given y = 3 when x = 0.

**Step 1:** Separate: dy = 2x dx.
**Step 2:** Integrate both sides: integral of dy = integral of 2x dx.
**Step 3:** y = x^2 + C.
**Step 4:** Use initial condition: 3 = 0^2 + C, so C = 3.

**Final Answer: y = x^2 + 3.**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The most common mistake is forgetting the constant of integration C. Every time you integrate, you MUST add + C. Without it, your general solution is incomplete and you'll lose marks. Also, when separating variables, make sure dy goes with the y terms and dx goes with the x terms. Mixing them up makes the equation unsolvable.
